ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a square with side length 100 cm, with the upper-right vertex labeled M and the lower-right vertex labeled N. Inside the square, a broken line is drawn starting from M, folding back and forth left and right and gradually downward. The 1 cm marked in the figure indicates that the vertical spacing between adjacent horizontal line segments is 1 cm; the bottom side is labeled 100 cm, and the left-side height is also labeled 100 cm. Reasoning: This broken line from M to N is composed of many horizontal segments and vertical connecting segments. Each horizontal segment spans the width of the square, so each horizontal segment is 100 cm long. Since the height of the square is 100 cm, and it descends 1 cm each time, there are 100 such horizontal crossings in total, while the total vertical descent length is 100×1=100 cm. The total horizontal length is 100×100=10000 cm. The total length of the broken line is 10000+100=10100 cm.

method.method_draft: Read the figure first: it shows a 100 cm by 100 cm square, with a zigzag/striped line starting at M on the top right and ending at N on the bottom right. The repeated labels 1 cm indicate that successive horizontal runs are spaced 1 cm apart vertically, so the drawn path fills the square in 1 cm steps from top to bottom. Then use the fact that the total length of a broken line is the sum of all its straight pieces. Here that means 100 horizontal traversals of length 100 cm plus 100 vertical connectors of length 1 cm, so the total is 100×100 + 100×1 = 10100 cm.
